phrases.phrase: Hello, how are you today?

alternatives.text: Hi, how are you today?
Hey, how are you today?

phrases.phrase: Good morning, it's nice to see you
phrases.grammar: Contraction tip: 'it's' = 'it is'. Never use 'its' (possessive) for this.

alternatives.text: Good morning, it's great to see you
Good morning, it's good to see you
Good morning, it's a pleasure to see you

translations.es: Buenos días, es un placer verte

phrases.phrase: Hi there, how's your day going?
phrases.grammar: 'How's' = 'How is'. Present continuous ('going') describes an ongoing state.

alternatives.text: Hey there, how's your day going?
Hello there, how's your day going?

phrases.phrase: Good afternoon, how have you been?
phrases.grammar: 'How have you been?' uses the present perfect to ask about a period up to now — not just this moment.

phrases.phrase: Hey, how's everything with you?

alternatives.text: Hi, how's everything with you?
Hello, how's everything with you?

phrases.phrase: Morning, hope you're doing well
phrases.grammar: Subject drop in casual speech: 'Morning, hope you're well' omits 'Good' and 'I' — common in informal greetings.

alternatives.text: Morning, I hope you're doing well

translations.es: Buenos días, espero que estés bien

phrases.phrase: Good evening, how's your day been?

translations.es: Buenas noches, ¿cómo ha estado tu día?

phrases.phrase: Hey, how's life treating you?
phrases.grammar: Idiomatic use: 'treat' here means 'to deal with / affect'. 'How is life treating you?' = 'Is life going well for you?'

alternatives.text: Hi, how's life treating you?
Hello, how's life treating you?

phrases.phrase: Hi, it's good to catch up with you
phrases.grammar: 'Catch up' (phrasal verb) = to exchange news after time apart. Common collocations: 'catch up with someone', 'catch up on news'.

alternatives.text: Hey, it's good to catch up with you
Hello, it's good to catch up with you

translations.es: Hola, es bueno ponerse al día contigo

phrases.phrase: Hello, how have you been lately?

alternatives.text: Hi, how have you been lately?
Hey, how have you been lately?

phrases.phrase: Hi there, hope you're having a good day

alternatives.text: Hey there, hope you're having a good day
Hello there, hope you're having a good day

translations.es: Hola, espero que tengas un buen día

phrases.phrase: Hey, what's new with you?

alternatives.text: Hi, what's new with you?
Hello, what's new with you?

phrases.phrase: Good morning, how's everything going?
Hi, how are you holding up?
phrases.grammar: 'Holding up' (phrasal verb) = coping, managing under pressure. Implies checking in with empathy.

alternatives.text: Hey, how are you holding up?
Hello, how are you holding up?

phrases.phrase: Hey there, how's your week been?

alternatives.text: Hi there, how's your week been?
Hello there, how's your week been?

phrases.phrase: Hello, hope you're doing fine

alternatives.text: Hi, hope you're doing fine
Hey, hope you're doing fine

phrases.phrase: Hi, it's been a while, how are you?
phrases.grammar: 'It's been a while' uses present perfect to connect the past to the present. Contrast: 'It was a while ago' (simple past — finished).

alternatives.text: Hey, it's been a while, how are you?
Hello, it's been a while, how are you?

translations.es: Hola, ha pasado un tiempo, ¿cómo estás?

phrases.phrase: Good afternoon, how's life treating you?

translations.es: Buenas tardes, ¿cómo te trata la vida?

phrases.phrase: Hey, nice to see you again, how have you been?

alternatives.text: Hi, nice to see you again, how have you been?
Hello, nice to see you again, how have you been?

translations.es: Oye, es bueno verte de nuevo, ¿cómo has estado?

phrases.phrase: It was great seeing you!
phrases.grammar: Exclamatory sentence: 'It was great seeing you!' uses the gerund after 'seeing'. Compare: 'It was great to see you!' — both correct, gerund is slightly more casual.

alternatives.text: It was great to see you!
It was good seeing you!
It was wonderful seeing you!

phrases.phrase: Take care of yourself!
phrases.grammar: 'Take care of yourself' uses a reflexive pronoun. 'Take care' alone is also common as a farewell.

alternatives.text: Take care!

phrases.phrase: Have a wonderful day!

alternatives.text: Have a great day!
Have a nice day!
Have a good day!

phrases.phrase: See you around!
phrases.grammar: 'See you around' implies you'll meet again without fixing a time. More casual than 'See you later' or 'See you soon'.

phrases.phrase: It was lovely to meet you
phrases.grammar: Note the difference: 'Nice to meet you' (first time) vs 'Nice to see you' (you've met before). Mixing them is a common mistake.

alternatives.text: It was nice to meet you
It was great to meet you
It was a pleasure to meet you

phrases.phrase: Don't be a stranger!
phrases.grammar: 'Don't be a stranger' is an idiomatic farewell meaning 'keep in touch / visit again'. Not literal.

phrases.phrase: We should do this again sometime
phrases.grammar: 'We should do this again' — modal 'should' here is a suggestion, not an obligation. Very common in social farewells.

phrases.phrase: It was a pleasure, hope to see you again

alternatives.text: It was a pleasure, I hope to see you again

translations.es: Fue un placer, espero verte de nuevo

phrases.phrase: Say hi to everyone for me
phrases.grammar: 'Say hi to everyone for me' — indirect greeting via a third person. 'Say hi', 'give my regards', 'send my love' vary in formality.

alternatives.text: Say hello to everyone for me

phrases.phrase: Take care and stay in touch
phrases.grammar: 'Stay in touch' (phrasal verb) = keep communicating. Synonyms: 'keep in touch', 'keep me posted'.

alternatives.text: Take care and keep in touch

phrases.phrase: It was so good catching up with you
phrases.grammar: 'Catch up' revisited: 'catching up' as a gerund after 'good'. Compare phrase 8: 'catch up with you'.

alternatives.text: It was so great catching up with you
It was good catching up with you

translations.es: Qué bueno fue ponernos al día

phrases.phrase: Nice to meet you, I'm glad we connected

alternatives.text: Nice to meet you, I'm glad we met

translations.es: Mucho gusto, me alegra que nos hayamos conocido

phrases.phrase: I could be better
phrases.grammar: 'Could be better' is a polite understatement meaning 'I'm not great'. English often uses understatement to avoid being negative.

phrases.phrase: How's your day been?
I've had a great day
phrases.grammar: Present perfect 'I've had' links a past event to the present feeling. Contrast: 'I had a great day' (simple past, already over).

phrases.phrase: How's your week been?
I've had better days
phrases.grammar: 'I've had better days' is an idiomatic understatement = 'today was bad'. Very common polite complaint.

phrases.phrase: I'm sad
I'm happy
I'm excited
I'm bored
I'm tired
I'm angry
I'm surprised
I'm confused
I'm worried
I'm nervous
I'm scared
I'm relaxed
I'm stressed
I'm busy
Why are you sad?
Why are you so happy?
phrases.grammar: 'So' as an intensifier: 'Why are you SO happy?' adds emphasis. It can also signal mild surprise.

phrases.phrase: Why are you excited?
Why are you bored?
Why are you tired?
Why are you angry?
Why are you surprised?
Why are you confused?
Why are you worried?
Why are you nervous?
Why are you scared?
Why are you relaxed?
Why are you stressed?
What's on your mind?
phrases.grammar: 'What's on your mind?' is an idiom meaning 'What are you thinking about / worried about?'

phrases.phrase: Is there anything I can do for you?
phrases.grammar: 'Is there anything I can do for you?' — formal offer of help. Informal version: 'Can I help you with anything?'

alternatives.text: Is there anything I can help you with?
Can I do anything for you?

translations.es: ¿Hay algo que pueda hacer por ti?

phrases.phrase: I'd like to introduce myself. I'm the new account manager for your region.

translations.es: Me gustaría presentarme. Soy la nueva gerente de cuentas para su región.

es.text: Me gustaría presentarme. Soy el nuevo gerente de cuentas para su región.

phrases.phrase: It was a pleasure meeting you. I'll follow up by email with the details.

translations.es: Fue un placer conocerle. Le enviaré un correo con los detalles que hablamos.

phrases.phrase: Please allow me to introduce Dr. Martínez, who will lead the session this afternoon.

translations.es: Permítame presentarle al Dr. Martínez, quien dirigirá la sesión de esta tarde.

es.text: Permítame presentarle a la Dra. Martínez, quien dirigirá la sesión de esta tarde.

phrases.grammar: 'Please allow me to introduce' — formal third-party introduction used in professional settings

phrases.phrase: I wanted to reach out and offer my sincere condolences on your loss.

translations.es: Quería comunicarme para ofrecerle mis más sinceras condolencias por su pérdida.

phrases.phrase: On behalf of the entire team, welcome aboard. We're thrilled to have you.

translations.es: En nombre de todo el equipo, bienvenido. Estamos encantados de tenerte con nosotros.

es.text: En nombre de todo el equipo, bienvenida. Estamos encantados de tenerte con nosotros.

phrases.phrase: I trust this message finds you well. I'm writing to follow up on last week's conversation.

translations.es: Espero que se encuentre bien. Le escribo para continuar con nuestra conversación de la semana pasada.

phrases.grammar: 'I trust this message finds you well' — formal epistolary opener used in professional correspondence

phrases.phrase: It is my pleasure to introduce our keynote speaker, whose work has shaped this field.

translations.es: Es un placer presentar a nuestra conferenciante principal, cuyo trabajo ha dado forma a este campo.

es.text: Es un placer presentar a nuestro conferenciante principal, cuyo trabajo ha dado forma a este campo.

phrases.phrase: I don't believe we've been formally introduced. I'm here representing the European delegation.

translations.es: Creo que no nos han presentado formalmente. Estoy aquí representando a la delegación europea.

phrases.grammar: 'I don't believe we've been formally introduced' — a polished way to initiate a first introduction in a formal setting

phrases.phrase: On behalf of the delegation, allow me to convey how delighted we are by this reception.

translations.es: En nombre de la delegación, permítame expresar lo encantados que estamos por esta recepción.

phrases.phrase: I appreciate you taking the time to meet with me, knowing how demanding your schedule is.

translations.es: Le agradezco que haya encontrado tiempo para reunirse conmigo, siendo tan exigente su agenda.

phrases.grammar: 'I appreciate you taking the time' — gerund after 'appreciate' expresses formal gratitude

phrases.phrase: It is with great honor that we welcome the distinguished delegates to this commemorative gathering.

translations.es: Es con gran honor que damos la bienvenida a los distinguidos delegados a esta reunión conmemorativa.

phrases.grammar: 'It is with great honor that' — cleft construction used in ceremonial or formal addresses

phrases.phrase: Cultural awareness in greetings is not merely etiquette; it signals respect for those you engage with.

translations.es: La conciencia cultural en los saludos no es solo protocolo; es una señal de respeto por los valores de quienes te rodean.

phrases.phrase: The protocol for introductions in this context requires that the senior representative speak first.

translations.es: El protocolo de presentaciones en este contexto exige que el representante de mayor rango hable primero.

phrases.grammar: 'requires that … speak' — formal subjunctive after verbs of requirement or mandate

phrases.phrase: I would be remiss not to acknowledge the immense contribution you have made to this institution.

translations.es: Sería una negligencia de mi parte no reconocer la inmensa contribución que ha aportado a esta institución.

phrases.grammar: 'I would be remiss not to' — formal expression of obligation to acknowledge or address something

phrases.phrase: Please accept my most sincere felicitations on the occasion of your well-deserved promotion.

translations.es: Por favor, acepte mis más sinceras felicitaciones con motivo de su tan merecido ascenso.

phrases.phrase: It's been ages! How have you been keeping?

translations.es: Hace siglos que no nos vemos. ¿Cómo has estado?

phrases.grammar: 'It's been ages' — present perfect to express a long elapsed time informally

phrases.phrase: I don't think we've met before. I'm [name].

translations.es: Creo que no nos conocemos. Soy [nombre].

phrases.phrase: What a small world! I had no idea you knew each other!

translations.es: ¡Qué pequeño es el mundo! No sabía que se conocían.

phrases.phrase: I've heard so much about you. It's great to finally meet you!

translations.es: He escuchado mucho sobre ti. ¡Es genial conocerte por fin!

phrases.grammar: 'I've heard' — present perfect for past experience relevant to the present moment

phrases.phrase: Let me introduce you to a colleague of mine.

translations.es: Déjame presentarte a un colega mío.

es.text: Déjame presentarte a una colega mía.

phrases.phrase: I hope I'm not interrupting. Do you have a moment?

translations.es: Espero no estar interrumpiendo. ¿Tienes un momento?

phrases.phrase: It was great catching up. We should do this more often.

translations.es: Fue genial ponernos al día. Deberíamos hacer esto más seguido.

phrases.grammar: 'Catching up' — gerund noun phrase for reconnecting after time apart

phrases.phrase: Please give my regards to your family.

translations.es: Saluda a tu familia de mi parte, por favor.

phrases.phrase: I wasn't expecting to see you here. What a pleasant surprise!

translations.es: No esperaba verte aquí. ¡Qué agradable sorpresa!

phrases.phrase: It's lovely to see you looking so well.
If you're ever in the city, don't hesitate to give me a call.

translations.es: Si alguna vez te encuentras en la ciudad, no dudes en llamarme.

phrases.grammar: 'If + present simple + imperative' for open-ended polite invitations

phrases.phrase: I believe we share a mutual acquaintance. You know [name] from the conference, I think?

translations.es: Creo que tenemos un conocido en común. ¿Conoces a [nombre] de la conferencia?

phrases.phrase: I must confess, I've been looking forward to this introduction. Your work precedes you.

translations.es: Debo confesarlo: esperaba con entusiasmo este encuentro. Su trabajo lo precede.
